Sathish Ninan, J.
The original petition filed by the husband against the wife, seeking dissolution of marriage alleging cruelty, was dismissed by the Family Court.
The husband is in appeal.
2. The marriage between the parties was solemnized on 06.09.2004.
The parties are living separately since the year 2013.
The husband alleged mental cruelty by the respondent-wife.
She refused residence at the matrimonial home along with his family members.
She always complained about his social status and used to insult him in public.
False complaints were lodged against him before the police, alleging harassment for dowry.
Accordingly he sought for dissolution of marriage.
The respondent-wife denied the allegations levelled.
It was alleged that the husband and his family members were ill-treating and harassing her.
4. The Family Court held that the husband failed to prove the allegations of mental cruelty.
Accordingly the original petition was dismissed.
5. We have heard Sri.M.Ramesh Chander, the learned Senior Counsel on behalf of the appellant-husband and Sri.T.Madhu, the learned counsel for the respondent- wife.
6. The Family Court found that the allegations of mental cruelty levelled by the husband are not proved.
It is to be noticed that, admittedly the wife had filed complaints against the husband under Section 498A IPC and under the Domestic Violence Act.
While she was examined as RW1, she deposed that the allegations made in such complaints were false.

The relevant deposition reads thus :-

Upon such complaint being lodged by the wife the husband had to suffer severe mental agony.
Crime No.906/2013 was registered against him at the Husdurg Police Station.
The husband had to suffer mental trauma consequent on the filing of such complaints which, the wife admitted to have been false allegations.
The said conduct by itself amounts to inflicting of mental cruelty on the spouse.

In Litty Mary John v.
Manoj K. Varghese (2024 (5) KLT 231), the court held that, "11. A single, overarching definition of "cruelty" is impractical and ineffective, as it can manifest in various forms and shapes - it may be perceived differently in different situations.

entities.text:
Litty Mary John v.
Manoj K. Varghese (2024 (5) KLT 231)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: What constitutes cruelty often differs from person to person, situation to situation, as it is subjective and depends on the perception of the individual experiencing it.
12. The concept of cruelty indubitably is inherently subjective - it being inevitable - since what one person considers cruel, may not be perceived the same way by another.
This subjectivity arises from individual 2025:KER:37128 differences in values, experiences, and sensitivity.
For instance, an action that causes emotional distress to one person, might be perceived as trivial or inconsequential by someone else.

These varying perceptions make it difficult to establish a universal definition of "cruelty", as it relies heavily on the individual's personal interpretation and emotional response to the behaviour in question."
In Latha Kunjamma v. Anil Kumar (2008 (2) KLT 545), it was held that making false allegations against the spouse amounts to mental cruelty.

entities.text: Latha Kunjamma v. Anil Kumar (2008 (2) KLT 545)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We are unable to agree with the Family Court in its finding that the husband failed to prove the allegation of cruelty.
7. The above apart, the parties have been living separately since the year 2013.
Admittedly the wife never initiated any steps for restitution of conjugal rights.
In Rajib Kumar vs. Sushmita Saha [(2023) 17 SCC 441], the Apex Court held that keeping the parties together despite irretrievable breakdown of marriage amounts to cruelty on both sides.

entities.text: Rajib Kumar vs. Sushmita Saha [(2023) 17 SCC 441]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such long separation without any intention to resume cohabitation amounts to cruelty on the spouse.

The Court held,
2025:KER:37128 "Continued bitterness, dead emotions and long separation, in the given facts and circumstances of a case, can be construed as a case of "irretrievable breakdown of marriage", which is also a facet of cruelty".
8.
We find that on the above grounds the appellant is entitled for a decree of divorce.
Resultantly, the appeal is allowed.
The decree and judgment of the Family Court are set aside.
The marriage between the appellant-petitioner and the respondent-wife will stand dissolved by a decree of divorce.
The original petition will stand allowed.
No costs.
